subject: physical-education
title: Concept model A: the technical model for the chosen activity
focus: the technical model for the chosen activity
essentialQuestion: What does real depth in one activity actually require?
materials: equipment for the chosen specialization or a substitute
privacySafeScenario: Run a documented development block in the chosen specialization: technical model, practice design, evidence of change, and an honest evaluation of what did not improve.
studentTask: Learner applies the technical model for the chosen activity in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind the technical model for the chosen activity and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the the technical model for the chosen activity task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: Any activity the learner can access and perform is a valid specialization, including adapted sport, seated activity, and self-designed movement practice.
extensionChallenge: Apply the technical model for the chosen activity under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Any activity the learner can access and perform is a valid specialization, including adapted sport, seated activity, and self-designed movement practice.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of the technical model for the chosen activity in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
